issues.t: VVT oil line bursts and dumps engine oil
issues.sym: A sudden, large oil leak, oil spraying under the hood or onto the road, a low oil pressure light, and smoke if oil hits the hot exhaust.
issues.why: Early V6 engines used a section of rubber hose in the oil line that feeds the variable valve timing system. The hose can split under pressure and the engine can lose most of its oil in seconds.
issues.next: If the oil light comes on, pull over and shut the engine off right away to avoid engine damage. Have the rubber-hose line replaced with Toyota's all-metal line, and ask a dealer about the ZE2 warranty program.

issues.t: Water pump leak on the V6
issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping, a pink or white crusty residue on the passenger side of the engine, a sweet smell, or a grinding noise from the pump area. Leaking coolant can wet the drive belt and make it slip.
issues.why: The water pump seal wears and starts to seep from the weep hole or gasket, usually somewhere around 80,000 to 130,000 miles. On the V6 the pump sits behind the timing cover area, so the repair is labor-heavy.
issues.next: Check the coolant tank level often and do not let the engine overheat. Have the pump replaced, ideally with the thermostat and drive belt at the same time, and use Toyota pink long-life coolant.

issues.t: Water pump leak on the 4-cylinder
issues.sym: Low coolant, pinkish residue around the water pump on the passenger side of the engine, and sometimes a grinding or whirring noise.
issues.why: The water pump seal and bearing wear out with age and mileage. The 4-cylinder pump is easier to reach than the V6 pump, so it is a smaller job.
issues.next: Keep the coolant topped up with Toyota long-life coolant and replace the pump before it fails completely or the engine overheats.

issues.t: Brief rattle on cold start
issues.sym: A loud knocking or rattling noise for about a second right after starting the engine, mostly after the car has sat overnight.
issues.why: The variable valve timing gear on the camshaft can let the camshaft move briefly before oil pressure builds. Toyota issued a service bulletin with an updated gear assembly.
issues.next: The noise is not immediately harmful, but have a Toyota dealer confirm it and replace the cam timing gear with the updated part.

issues.t: Oil consumption at higher mileage
issues.sym: The oil level drops between changes and you need to add oil, sometimes with blue smoke at startup or a low oil warning.
issues.why: As these engines age, worn piston rings and valve seals let more oil burn in the cylinders. Owners report it on both the 4-cylinder and the V6.
issues.next: Check the oil every few fill-ups and top it up. If you are adding more than a quart every 1,200 miles or so, have a shop or dealer run an oil consumption test.

issues.t: Hesitation or jerky shifts when accelerating
issues.sym: The car hesitates, jerks or surges when you press the gas, or the engine speed rises and falls unevenly while the transmission shifts.
issues.why: Hesitant shifting on the 6-speed automatic is a known complaint on these Venzas. Old or low fluid, software and internal wear can all play a part.
issues.next: Have the transmission scanned for codes and the fluid checked. Ask a dealer whether a software update applies before agreeing to major transmission work.

issues.t: Warped front brake rotors
issues.sym: The steering wheel or brake pedal shakes or pulses when stopping, especially from highway speed.
issues.why: Owners of early Venzas report front rotors that warp or wear unevenly well before the pads are worn out. Uneven lug nut tightening can make it worse.
issues.next: Have the rotors measured. They usually need to be resurfaced or replaced along with the pads, and the wheels should be tightened with a torque wrench.

issues.t: Rattle from the steering column
issues.sym: A rattling or clunking noise from the steering column area when turning or driving over rough roads.
issues.why: Toyota issued a service bulletin for rattles inside the steering column on early Venzas. The fix is a revised column assembly.
issues.next: Have a dealer confirm the noise comes from the column and check whether the bulletin repair applies. It is mostly an annoyance, but get loose steering parts ruled out.

issues.t: Panoramic glass roof shatters
issues.sym: A loud bang while driving and broken glass falling from the roof, often with no obvious impact.
issues.why: Owners have reported the large glass roof panel shattering on its own. Thin tempered glass with built-in stress can break suddenly.
issues.next: Pull over safely and cover the opening. Report it to NHTSA and to Toyota, and check whether your insurance glass coverage applies.

issues.t: Humming wheel bearing
issues.sym: A humming or growling noise that gets louder with speed and changes when you turn or change lanes.
issues.why: A front or rear wheel bearing has worn out. The noise usually starts quietly and grows over time.
issues.next: Have the bearing checked soon. A badly worn bearing can get loose and affect handling, so do not wait for it to get loud.

issues.t: Worn front struts
issues.sym: A bouncy or floaty ride, the nose diving under braking, clunks over bumps, or oil on the strut bodies.
issues.why: The front struts wear out at higher mileage, and the large wheels on the Venza make the ride firm to begin with.
issues.next: Have the struts inspected. They are normally replaced in pairs, followed by a wheel alignment.

issues.t: Check engine light from a failed air-fuel sensor
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, sometimes with slightly worse fuel economy. Codes such as P0138, P0161 or P0057 are common.
issues.why: The air-fuel ratio sensor or oxygen sensor in the exhaust, or its heater circuit, wears out with age.
issues.next: Have the codes read to see which sensor failed. It is not urgent, but fix it before an emissions test and so fuel economy does not suffer.

issues.t: ABS light from a wheel speed sensor
issues.sym: The ABS and traction control lights come on and stay on. The normal brakes still work.
issues.why: One of the wheel speed sensors or its wiring has failed. The anti-lock and stability systems switch off when they lose a sensor signal.
issues.next: Have the ABS codes read to find which wheel is affected. The sensor itself is usually a simple part.

issues.t: Tire pressure light from corroded sensors
issues.sym: The tire pressure light stays on or flashes even when the tires are properly inflated.
issues.why: The tire pressure sensors inside the wheels use metal valve stems that corrode, and their internal batteries eventually die.
issues.next: Check all tire pressures first. If they are correct, have the sensors tested and replace the faulty ones, ideally when tires are changed.

issues.t: No-start from corroded battery terminals
issues.sym: Clicking or no crank when you turn the key, flickering lights, or odd electrical behavior that comes and goes.
issues.why: Corrosion on the battery terminals or a weak battery stops enough current from reaching the starter.
issues.next: Clean and tighten the battery terminals and have the battery tested. Replace it if it fails the test.

issues.t: Factory alarm goes off by itself
issues.sym: The car alarm sounds randomly, often at night, with no one near the car.
issues.why: The hood latch switch can falsely report that the hood is open. Toyota released a revised hood latch assembly.
issues.next: Have the hood latch switch checked and replaced with the updated latch if it is the cause.

issues.t: Check engine light from the gas cap or EVAP system
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, often with an evaporative emissions code such as P0441 or P0455, with no change in how the car drives.
issues.why: A worn or loose gas cap seal lets fuel vapor escape, which the evaporative emissions system reports as a leak.
issues.next: Tighten the cap until it clicks. If the light returns, replace the cap with a Toyota one and have the EVAP system smoke-tested if the code comes back.

issues.t: Accelerator pedal can be trapped by the floor mat (recall)
issues.sym: The gas pedal sticks down or will not return, and the car keeps accelerating.
issues.why: An unsecured or wrong floor mat can slide forward and trap the accelerator pedal.
issues.next: Remove any loose or stacked floor mats now. Have a Toyota dealer confirm the recall repair was done. It is free.

issues.t: Brake lights may not work (recall)
issues.sym: Brake lights do not come on when you press the pedal, warning lights appear, or the car may be hard to shift out of Park or start.
issues.why: Silicone grease on the brake light switch can build up resistance in the contacts, which can stop the brake lights from working.
issues.next: Have someone confirm your brake lights work. Ask a Toyota dealer to check for open recall 12V-091; the switch repair is free.

issues.t: Seat heater wiring can short and burn (recall)
issues.sym: The heated seat stops working, feels too hot in one spot, or you smell burning from the seat.
issues.why: Compressing the seat cushion over time can damage the seat heater wires, causing a short that can burn the occupant.
issues.next: Stop using the seat heater until a Toyota dealer checks the recall (14V-743). The repair is free.

issues.t: A/C drain leak can wet the airbag computer (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light comes on, there is water on the floor, or in rare cases an airbag deploys unexpectedly.
issues.why: A blocked A/C drain hose can let condensation drip onto the airbag control module, which can short circuit and disable the airbags or set them off.
issues.next: Have a Toyota dealer confirm recall 13V-442 is complete. The fix is free. Get any wet carpet or airbag light checked right away.

issues.t: Driver door wiring can disable side airbags (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light comes on, often after the driver door has been opened and closed many times.
issues.why: The airbag wiring that runs into the driver door can wear through from repeated door use. That can disable the driver-side side and curtain airbags.
issues.next: Have a Toyota dealer check for recall 21V-257. The wiring repair is free and important for side-impact protection.

issues.t: Passenger airbag sensor not recalibrated after accessories (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag status light may show the wrong state for who is sitting in the seat.
issues.why: On cars that had dealer accessories such as seat covers fitted, the passenger seat occupant sensor may not have been recalibrated, so the airbag may not deploy correctly.
issues.next: Ask a Toyota dealer to check recall 13V-014 with your VIN. The inspection and recalibration are free.

issues.t: Windshield cracks from small stone chips
issues.sym: A small chip from a stone quickly spreads into a long crack across the windshield, sometimes within days of the hit.
issues.why: Many owners of the second-generation Venza report the windshield cracking far more easily than expected from minor stone strikes.
issues.next: Get chips repaired right away before they spread. Check whether your insurance covers glass, and use original glass so the front camera can be recalibrated.

issues.t: 12-volt battery drains while parked
issues.sym: The car will not start or power on after sitting for a day or two, even when nearly new, and needs a jump start.
issues.why: The connected-services module (DCM) can stay awake after the car is turned off and slowly drain the small 12-volt battery. Toyota issued a bulletin and a software update.
issues.next: Have the 12-volt battery tested and ask a Toyota dealer about the DCM software update. Driving the car regularly or using a battery maintainer helps in the meantime.

issues.t: Shadows from low-beam headlights
issues.sym: At night the low beams cast dark shadows or bands on the road that can look like objects or animals. They go away on high beam.
issues.why: Owners trace it to the LED headlight design and its internal beam shutter. Toyota has not issued a recall.
issues.next: Have the headlight aim checked by a dealer. Report the problem to NHTSA so it is on record.

issues.t: Milky oil and low oil pressure warning in cold weather
issues.sym: An "Oil Pressure Low" message, a check engine light, or milky, light-colored oil on the dipstick or oil cap, usually in very cold weather.
issues.why: On short trips in extreme cold, moisture from the engine condenses in the oil and can freeze, which can drop oil pressure. Toyota issued a service bulletin for these engines.
issues.next: Have a dealer check the oil and the codes and follow the bulletin. Longer drives that fully warm the engine help keep moisture out of the oil.

issues.t: Check engine light from an EVAP valve or tank pressure sensor
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with codes P24517F or P14502A, and the car drives normally.
issues.why: A valve in the fuel vapor system can stick, or the fuel tank pressure sensor can report a stuck signal. Toyota issued a bulletin for these hybrids.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask a dealer about the bulletin repair. This is usually not urgent, but it can fail an emissions test.

issues.t: Musty smell or wet floor from a blocked A/C drain
issues.sym: A musty or moldy smell from the vents, fogging windows, or water on the front passenger floor.
issues.why: The A/C drain hose can get blocked, sometimes by insect nests, so condensation backs up inside the car. Toyota has bulletins on blocked drains and on cleaning up musty odors after water gets in.
issues.next: Have the A/C drain cleared and any wet carpet dried. Replace the cabin air filter and ask about Toyota's odor treatment.

issues.t: Damaged cover on the rear motor wiring connector
issues.sym: Usually no symptom; the damage is found during service or after hitting road debris. In rare cases a hybrid system warning may appear if water reaches the connector.
issues.why: The plastic cover over the rear electric motor wiring connector under the car can get damaged. Toyota issued a technical tip on it for these hybrids.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to inspect the cover at your next service and replace it if it is cracked.

issues.t: Rear turn signals can short from moisture (recall)
issues.sym: A rear turn signal stops working or flashes fast, or there is fogging inside the rear lamp.
issues.why: Moisture can get inside the rear turn signal LEDs and condense on the circuit board, causing a short.
issues.next: Have a Toyota dealer check for recall 22V-033. The repair is free.

issues.t: Stability control may stay off after restart (recall)
issues.sym: If you switched stability control off, it may still be off the next time you start the car instead of turning back on.
issues.why: A software error in the skid control computer can stop the stability control system from re-enabling.
issues.next: Have a Toyota dealer check recall 22V-239 and update the software for free. Until then, check that the VSC off light is not on after starting.

issues.t: Instrument panel may not show speed or warning lights (recall)
issues.sym: At startup the gauge display may fail to show your speed, brake system warnings or the tire pressure warning.
issues.why: A software error in the instrument panel can stop it from displaying key information when the car is started.
issues.next: Have a Toyota dealer check recall 25V-595 and update the software. It is free.

issues.t: Backup camera may freeze or go blank (recall)
issues.sym: The rearview camera picture freezes or the screen stays blank when you shift into reverse.
issues.why: A software error in the camera system on vehicles with the Panoramic View Monitor can freeze or blank the image.
issues.next: Check around the car before reversing until fixed, and have a Toyota dealer apply the free software update for recall 25V-744.
